title: In the mouse caudoputamen, where cell types are uniform, the voxel input map did not predict local task coding beyond a calibrated null, except for feedback (IBL, 2,646 units)
abstract: Question: across mouse brain regions, axonal input predicts task coding, but input and cell-type mix change together. Does the input map predict coding inside one region whose cell types are nearly uniform? Data: IBL Brain-Wide Map spike times of 2,646 good caudoputamen (CP) units (74 probes, 69 sessions) and of 31,439 units in 60 regions (344 probes); the Knox 2019 voxel connectome (100 um); published BWM region decoding scores; Allen MERFISH cell types. Method (plan frozen before analysis): for each unit, condition-combined selectivity for stimulus side, choice, feedback and block prior. For each unit voxel, the input-weighted mean BWM score of each variable over all source regions. The statistic is the variable-specific match (unit and variable fixed effects, distance control). Null A permutes source scores within divisions and keeps the input topography. Results: in CP, the match was beta 0.049 (session bootstrap CI 0.003 to 0.086), but null A gave p = 0.082, so the hypothesis was not supported. On 200 smooth synthetic maps, null A had 7% false positives; a planned distance-rewiring null had 39% and is not valid. Exploratory: feedback selectivity matched its input map (beta 0.17, Holm p = 0.012; 0.20 to 0.26 with position controls), choice weakly, stimulus not, and block prior in the opposite direction. MERFISH composition was nearly uniform across CP bins (Bhattacharyya 0.97). The brain-wide within-region test was also not supported (beta 0.014, p = 0.051), but feedback matched there too (p = 0.007; 0.016 without CP). Limitations: a weak CP coding map (split-half 0.19), an interpolated connectome, source scores from the same data set, and exploratory per-variable results.

display.caption: Top: CP maps (top view, 300 um bins; square size = unit count) of the input-predicted map X and of observed selectivity relative to the unit mean, for feedback and choice. Bottom left: H1 beta against null A (calibrated) and null B (not calibrated), with the session bootstrap 95% CI. Bottom right: false-positive rates of the two nulls on 200 smooth synthetic maps without wiring dependence.

Left (exploratory): beta per variable in CP with null A 95% ranges, with distance control only, plus linear position, plus quadratic position; Holm-corrected p. Middle: S3 sensitivity variants of the pooled test with null A ranges and one-sided p. Right (exploratory): correlation of X with the cross-session smoothed CP selectivity map, per variable.

S1 brain-wide within-region test (344 probes). Left: pooled beta against null A. Middle (exploratory): within-region beta per region with its null A mean. Right (exploratory): per-variable betas for 60 regions and for 59 regions without CP, with null A 95% ranges and uncorrected p.

citations.reason: We use its input-weighted source-encoding predictor at the 100 um voxel scale. Inside the caudoputamen the general variable-specific match did not pass a calibrated null; only feedback coding matched.

It found that input wiring, not cell-type mix, predicts region-level coding, mostly through feedback decoding. Inside a region with uniform cell types, we find the same feedback specificity, but no general match.
We reuse its shared helper code (ontology, Knox loading, mapper) and its motivation: input and cell-type similarity are confounded across regions.
Our calibration shows that distance-rewired nulls are also liberal at the voxel scale inside one region (39% false positives).
